Verified facts that drive the scores (read-only, this checkout):
- cacheKey = sha256(identitySalt\0versionSalt\0diffText) with NO mode salt (gate-engine/review/reviewers.mts:441-455); planReviewWork keys `${salt}|split:<group>` (lens/split.mts:341) — the split precedent already proves mode-in-key is the kill-switch idiom.
- PASS write path: settle.mts:77 savePasses({[t.key]: {at, model, duration_ms, lens fields}}); FAIL/inconclusive never cached; archiveFailedDiff on fail (settle.mts:79).
- Store: one `.devkit/review-cache.json` per repo anchored at git-common-dir → shared by ALL worktrees/branches (verdict-store.mts:91-104); MAX_ENTRIES=100 is a module const shared by all four stores (verdict-store.mts:38, applied in saveEntries:176 via retainNewest, store-retention.mts:27-39, which emits cache_evicted). Retention doc says ~10 keys/attempt and zero evicted-then-needed TODAY — both incremental (≈+9 memory entries/attempt) and chunk (≈13+ keys + plan entries/attempt) change that; chunk at least raises the cap (but must make it per-store).
- Session fence: 4 stores hardcoded in cli/lib/ship/review/cache/session.mts:21-26 and `[ "${CACHE_FIELDS[1]}" = 4 ]` in review-target.sh:730-734 — any new store (incremental PR5) must touch both; both plans that stay inside review-cache.json avoid this.
- diffCacheIdentity (judge/diff-focus.mts:131-175) drops context/line numbers/index shas per file, so per-file identity is a sound, already-shipped primitive for all three plans.
- Correctness domain 'all' files are source-only, test-free (reviewers.mts:234-239) → incremental's "unlexable → full" fallback rarely fires for correctness (good for savings, but means the es-module-lexer guard IS the recall guard there); es-module-lexer is in `dependencies` (package.json:88) though dist-integrity.mts:102-103 documents it as dev-only intent.
- Judge stdin = buildCappedDiffEvidence(gitCached(cwd,[],files), stat) with 60000/8000/40 caps (diff-evidence.mts:85-87, run-review.mts:205) — the seam measure-first and chunk both exploit; run-review.mts:387 computes one diff per reviewer over s.files.

Kill-switch verdicts:
- incremental-first: NOT fully real. Under `on`, a delta-judged task still saves the whole-diff key (settle.mts:77 uses t.key; plan keeps whole-diff key "still saved"), so `off` replays partial-judgement PASSes on a byte-identical reship; revocation requires clear-cache (repo-wide, all branches). Also PR1 "off" mints memory into the shared 100-cap store — a silent eviction cost while nominally dark.
- chunk-fanout: REAL. `|chunk:` suffix + C=1 no-suffix makes on/off verdicts non-interchangeable and today's keys byte-identical; no clear-cache needed. The cost is the blast radius: checklist.mjs asset change (4 synced copies → identitySalt flip for every consumer), state-file path change, MAX_ENTRIES raise on a shared const, 3C+1 judges vs sc-1476 compliance, +17-35% attempt-1 cost, and predicted cross-chunk loss on state/concurrency lenses (SWE-PRBench Type2/3) behind a too-weak 'B ≥ A−1 row' guardrail.
- measure-first: REAL by construction — no gate code until E0/E1/E2 gate it; P1's `|file:<path>` keys are mode-distinct; PR1 is additive telemetry.

Silent recall reducers ranked: chunk (cross-chunk state/concurrency, dedup/≤12-line report truncating disclosure) > incremental (unresolved module graph → missed edges, transitive reuse compounding, non-import coupling, prompt nudging judge away from 'unchanged' files; mitigated by shadow-skip-miss) > measure-first (none in the gate; P1 later lacks an import guard and must graft incremental's).

Winner: measure-first (27) — highest evidence fit (E0 $0 audit decides whether ANY windowing matters, directly testing the CRITIQUE counterargument that the loop is serial disclosure + 14% false-block), lowest gate risk (nothing ships ungated, kill switches real), moderate cost (real $ but no engine surgery).
